instructions: Put the bulgur in a large bowl and pour 1 1/2 cups of hot water over it. Cover the bowl and let it stand for 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, finely chop the onion. Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and 1/4 tsp of the salt and cook, stirring now and then, for 6 to 8 minutes, until it's soft and golden at the edges.
Add the paprika and the cumin and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells toasty.
Add the beef, 1/2 tsp of the salt and the black pepper. Turn the heat up to medium-high and break the meat up with a spoon. Cook for 6 to 7 minutes, until it's browned and the pan is dry.
Transfer the filling to a plate and spread it out. Let it cool for at least 15 minutes. A hot filling tears the shells.

Add the egg, the flour and 3/4 tsp of the salt to the soaked bulgur. Knead with wet hands for 5 minutes, until the dough holds together and stops sticking to your hands. If it sticks, wet your hands again.
Put a large pot of water on to boil with 1 tbsp of the salt.

Pinch off a walnut-sized piece of dough, about 18 in all. Press your thumb into the middle and turn it to make a hollow with thin walls. Spoon in about 2 tsp of the filling, pinch the opening closed, and shape it into an oval. Set it on a tray and repeat with the rest.
Boil the kofte in two batches. They're done when they float, about 8 to 10 minutes. Keep each batch in the water for 2 minutes after it floats, then lift it out with a slotted spoon onto a plate.

Drizzle the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil over the kofte and squeeze half the lemon over the top. Cut the other half into wedges. Serve with the lemon wedges, and put the red pepper flakes on the table for anyone who wants heat.

To make a batch ahead, shape the kofte and freeze them on a tray until firm, then move them to a freezer bag for up to 3 months. Boil them straight from frozen until they float, about 12 to 14 minutes, then keep them in the water for 2 minutes. Boiled kofte keep in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat them on a baking sheet in a 350°F oven for 15 minutes.
method_notes: Gurmion (4.8 from 445) leads: a flour and egg bulgur shell, a beef and onion filling, shells boiled until they float. Walnuts, the usual filling, are left out so the dish stays nut-free, and the butter is olive oil so it stays dairy-free. The paprika and cumin come from Savor and Sizzle, and the freezer and lemon notes from Savor and Sizzle and Vidar Bergum. Boiling rather than deep frying is the lead's choice and the only version a weeknight cook will finish; it takes about 75 minutes, so it is a make-ahead batch rather than a 30 minute lunch.
